🟠 Nine Major Firms Launch $15M Bitcoin Security Consortium

BlackRock, Coinbase, Strategy, Fidelity Digital Assets, Anchorage Digital, ARK Invest, Block, Blockstream, and Galaxy have formed the Bitcoin Security Consortium, pledging $15 million over three years to fund open-source developers and advance quantum-resistant security research for the Bitcoin network.

Announced July 23, the consortium will direct funding independently, with members taking no role in Bitcoin governance or protocol decisions. Research priorities include post-quantum cryptography and long-term network resilience against potential future quantum-computing threats.

The initiative reflects growing institutional concern over quantum computing's long-term risk to Bitcoin's cryptographic foundations, with participants spanning Wall Street asset managers, crypto exchanges, and infrastructure providers.

The chairman of the Joint Chiefs warned that renewed heavy fighting could dangerously deplete Patriot interceptor stocks in theater. In plain terms: the pause isn’t about strategy or diplomacy. It’s about not running out of missiles.

That technical denial doesn’t change the outcome. This is the second straight night without US strikes inside Iran, and Iranian channels note with satisfaction that Tehran is also holding its fire. 

The story is spreading fast across Iranian media and the broader “Axis of Resistance” ecosystem, and that audience treats it as the only professional verdict that matters: Washington blinked because its magazine isn’t bottomless.

Around that pause, the machinery keeps moving. Tanker and transport aircraft are still cycling through the region, but the airlift is noticeably thinner than the surges that preceded earlier operations. 

Israel’s security system is sitting in “hold” — readiness at a high alert tier, where one phone call turns the whole machine back on. 

Oman‑mediated talks remain in the air, but seasoned officials assume the Iranians are doing what they always do: stretching time, offering no concrete concession, waiting to see what Trump brings to the table after his meeting with Netanyahu — or whether the choreography is already agreed.

So the battlefield logic today looks like this. The US can escalate, but every extra wave of attacks eats into the very defenses meant to protect its bases and allies.

Iran can keep stalling, but every day of relative quiet lets it test how far American patience and stockpiles go. 

Trump says he’s “not finished” with Iran and that “next week gets really bad for them” if they don’t talk. His generals are quietly telling him that “really bad” has a logistics cost.
